div.l: Poynant and sharp / and redy al his gere
His table dormant in his halle alway
Stode redy coủered al the longe day
At Sessions there was he lord and sire
Ful ofte tyme he was knyght of the Shire
An anlas and a gipser al of silk
Heeng at his girdel white as morne milk
A Shirreue hadde he ben and accomptoᵘur
Was nowher such a worthy vauasour
An habirdassher and a carpenter
A Webbe a dyer and a Tapicer
And they were clothed alle in o lyuere
Of a solempne and a greet frat̉ernite
Ful fressh and newe her gere apyked was
Her knyues nere nought chaped with bras
But al with siluer wrought ful clene and wel
Her girdeles and her powches eủerydel
Wel semed ech of hem a fair burgeys
To sitten in yildehalle on a deys
Eủerich for the wisdam that he can
Was shaply for to ben an alderman
For catel hadde they y nough an rente
And eke her wyues / wolde it wel assente
And ellis certeyne they were to blame
It is ful fair to be cleped madame
And gon to vigilies al bifore
And haue a mantel rialliche ybore
A Cook they hadde with hem for the nones
To boyle the chikenes with the maribones
And pouder marchant tart and galingale
Wel cowde he knowe a draught of londoıı̄un ale
He cowde roste and and broyle and frye
Maken mortreux / and wel bake a pye
But greet harme was it as it thoughte me
That on his shyne a mormal hadde he
For blank manger / þat made he with the beste
A Shipman was there wonynge fer by weste
For ought I woot he was of dertemouthe
He rood vpon a Rouncy / as he cowthe
